benefits: Completely private — the PDF never leaves your device; the encryption module is bundled with the site and runs locally.
Real AES-256 encryption — the PDF standard's strongest protection, readable by Adobe Reader and others.
Two passwords: a user password to open the file, and an optional owner password for permissions.

faqs.a: User password: anyone opening the PDF must type it. Owner password: controls permissions like printing and copying; if you leave it empty, your user password doubles as the owner password.
faqs.q: User password vs owner password — what is the difference?

faqs.a: AES-256, the strongest encryption the PDF standard defines. It is the same level banks and governments use for documents.
Yes. The encryption follows the PDF standard, so Adobe Reader, Preview, Chrome, Edge and mobile readers all ask for the password normally.
faqs.q: Will Adobe Reader open the protected file?

faqs.a: Yes. The encryption module (@cantoo/pdf-lib, a pdf-lib fork with encryption support) is bundled with the site, so protection works fully offline. Your document itself is never uploaded anywhere.
No — and neither can we. Passwords are typed into your browser and used only for the encryption step. If you lose the password, the file cannot be recovered. Write it down somewhere safe.
faqs.q: Can you recover my password if I forget it?

faqs.a: No. The entire process happens locally in your browser. Your document never leaves your device.
faqs.q: Is my file uploaded to a server?

protect-pdf.formula:
protected PDF = original content encrypted with AES-256
open password → user password    permissions password → owner password
howTo: Click “Choose PDF file” and select the PDF you want to protect.
Type a user password (at least 4 characters) — this is what readers will ask for.
Optionally set a different owner password and adjust printing/copying permissions.
Click “Protect PDF” and wait for the encryption to finish.
Download the protected PDF and test it: open it and confirm it asks for your password.
keyFacts: PDF encryption scrambles every string and stream in the file with AES-256; without the password the content is unreadable.
The user password gates opening; the owner password gates permissions like printing and copying.
Permissions are enforced by PDF readers on the honor system — most respect them, but they are not unbreakable locks.
This tool uses @cantoo/pdf-lib (a pdf-lib fork with encryption support), bundled with the site.
After encrypting, the tool re-opens the file with your password to verify the protection worked.
